The 156th Wing Staff Agencies (WSA) and the 156th Comptroller Flight (156 CPTF) serve as the executive decision-making, regulatory, and financial foundation of the 156th Wing, Puerto Rico Air National Guard (PRANG) based out of Muñiz Air National Guard Base, Carolina, Puerto Rico. 

Working directly in support of the Wing Commander, these sections maintain military readiness, safeguard resources, protect civil liberties, and manage base-wide operations.

meta.activeShooterMethods:
In an active shooter emergency, it is critical to remain calm and take the most reasonable action to protect your life.

Run (Escape): If a safe route is available, evacuate immediately. Leave belongings behind, help others if possible, and call 911 or the local equivalent once safe.

Hide (Barricade): If evacuation is not possible, move out of view, lock or block doors, turn off lights, silence devices, and remain quiet.

Fight (Take Action): Only as a last resort, when life is in imminent danger, attempt to disrupt or incapacitate the threat. (Use whatever means possible to overpower the shooter and save your life) 

Always follow directions and comply with law-enforcement instructions, keep hands visible, and proceed to the designated assembly area when directed.

When reporting information to the authorities, provide the threat’s location, description, weapons, number of individuals involved, and potential victims if known. 

At all times, follow local lockdown and emergency-notification procedures.

Reference: AFI 91-202_ANGSUP, The US Air Force Mishap Prevention Program

- Paragraph 1.6.28.7.1.

The method of documentation is up to the supervisor, if not otherwise prescribed by the applicable MAJCOM or related chain of authority. Options may include, but are not limited to, the DAF Form 55, Employee Safety and Health Record, electronic mediums such as AFFORMs/CAMs/CAS- B/GO81 or locally developed products. If the DAF Form 55, Employee Safety and Health Record is mandated for use as the training documentation device, the entity that mandated the form usage will prescribe the requirement in writing to include if signatures are required or optional. Regardless of the method chosen, documentation will contain the following minimum data: trainee name (last, first, middle initial), type of training and date of training. Neither the trainer or trainee signature is required unless specified in writing by the applicable chain of authority. NOTE: If the Integrated Maintenance Data System (IMDS), Core Automated Maintenance System (CAMS), etc., cannot support minimum documentation requirements, then they are not suitable as a documentation product.

meta.riskManagementNotes: Risk Management Fundamentals: Reference: DAFSMS and local RM program guidance. Address hazard identification, control selection, local escalation expectations, and when RM refresher training must be completed for this work center. Risk Management (RM) is a continuous and systematic process designed to preserve combat readiness and enhance force protection by proactively identifying, assessing, and mitigating operational hazards. I have structured this framework around four foundational principles: accepting no unnecessary risk, ensuring decisions are made at the appropriate command authority, integrating assessment early into mission planning, and maintaining continuous application throughout the operational lifecycle. This cycle is executed through a structured five-step methodology that begins with the identification of real or potential hazards, followed by a detailed assessment of their probability and severity to determine overall risk levels. Once identified, leaders develop and implement mitigation controls—such as engineering, administrative, or protective measures—and continuously supervise operations to evaluate control efficacy and adjust for emerging variables in the environment. To facilitate this process, the Joint Risk Assessment Tool (JRAT) serves as the primary web-based, automated platform managed by the U.S. Army Combat Readiness Center (USACRC) for standardizing risk management across the Department of War. This centralized system automates the generation of the DD Form 2977 (Deliberate Risk Assessment Worksheet) and provides specialized portals for each service branch to ensure alignment with joint standards and mishap statistics. I should note that JRAT streamlines the assessment process by offering pre-populated libraries of mission types and hazards, incorporating real-world lessons learned from historical data, and enabling global coordination for joint operations. By leveraging this tool, personnel can ensure their risk assessments are data-driven, compliant, and effectively integrated into the mission planning process to fortify force protection.

selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Train each affected worker on when PPE is necessary, what PPE is necessary, how to properly don, doff, adjust, and wear PPE, the limitations of assigned PPE, and the proper care, maintenance, useful life, and disposal of PPE. Require workers to demonstrate understanding and proper use before performing work requiring PPE, and retrain when workplace conditions, job assignments, PPE types, or worker knowledge gaps make prior training obsolete.
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use the work-center JHA, BE occupational health assessment, manufacturer instructions, DAFMAN 91-203 Chapter 14, and local safety office guidance to identify PPE requirements. Supervisors must ensure PPE is provided, used, cleaned, inspected, maintained in sanitary and serviceable condition, and documented in JSTO training records. Cover eye and face protection, head protection, foot protection, hand protection, protective clothing, and respiratory or hearing protection when those programs apply.
selectedModules.notes:
Personal Protective Equipment (PPE): 
This section details the specific **Lawn Care & Pressure Washing PPE** guidelines and **Cleaning Chemical PPE** availability protocols to be included directly in your Job Safety Training Outline (JSTO), aligned with **DAFMAN 91-203**. 

🧯 Task-Specific PPE Guidelines (JSTO Topic Integration) While administrative personnel within the Wing Staff Agencies and CPTF are primarily office-bound, certain groundskeeping, facility maintenance, and common-area cleaning tasks carry specific hazard exposure risks that mandate the use of personal protective equipment (PPE). 
--- 🟢 1. Power Lawn Equipment & Pressure Washer PPE Anytime personnel operate or assist near high-decibel lawn machinery or high-pressure washers, the following specialized PPE **must be utilized** to prevent hearing loss, physical trauma, and eye damage: 
* **Hearing Conservation (Ear Protection): 
** * **Applicability: 
** Mandatory when operating or working in the immediate vicinity of noise-hazardous equipment exceeding **85 dBA** (such as lawn trimmers, leaf blowers, and gas-powered pressure washers). * **Requirement: 
** Use only **serviceable, clean, and properly fitted** earplugs or earmuffs. 
* **Eye & Face Protection: 
** * **Lawn Trimmers / Leaf Blowers: 
** High-impact safety glasses or a full-face shield to protect against high-velocity thrown objects (rocks, twigs, and dust). * **Water Pressure Washers: 
** Sealed safety goggles (to prevent high-velocity water blowback and debris splash). 
* **Hand & Foot Protection: 
** * **Gloves: 
** Heavy-duty leather work gloves to prevent abrasions, severe vibration fatigue, and blisters. 
* **Footwear: 
** Sturdy, closed-toe leather boots (steel-toe safety shoes are highly recommended to prevent projectile impact and accidental high-pressure water injection injuries). 
--- 🧹 2. Office Cleaning Chemicals & Common Areas Exposure to everyday cleaning agents and disinfectants utilized in breakrooms, restrooms, and administrative common areas can cause severe skin irritation, chemical burns, or dermatitis. 
* **Hand Protection (Nitrile Gloves): 
** * **Applicability: 
** Nitrile gloves **must be worn** when handling any concentrated or diluted chemical cleaners, bleach, or sanitizing agents. 
* **Why Nitrile** Nitrile provides superior chemical resistance, puncture resistance, and does not carry the allergy risks associated with latex. * **Local Supply & Availability: 
** * **How to Access: ** Highly durable, disposable, and chemical-resistant **nitrile gloves are readily available at the 156th Wing Safety Office**. 
* **Action for Staff: 
** Prior to conducting any deep cleaning, spill response, or common area sanitation, coordinate with the Wing Safety Office or your Facility Manager to obtain your personal safety gloves.
